description: The GNU implementation of the AWK programming language.

tip: Signal the end of the command-line options, so later arguments are not treated as options even if they begin with -.

option.name: --assign
tip: Set the variable var to the value val before execution of the program begins.
The value is available inside the BEGIN rule.

option.name: --bignum
tip: Select arbitrary-precision arithmetic on numbers.
Has no effect if gawk is not compiled to use the GNU MPFR and MP libraries.

option.name: --characters-as-bytes
tip: Treat all input data as single-byte characters, and write print and printf output as single-byte characters.

option.name: --copyright
tip: Print the short version of the General Public License and exit.

option.name: --csv
tip: Enable special processing for files with comma separated values (CSV).
Cannot be combined with --posix; using both is a fatal error.

option.name: --debug
tip: Enable debugging of awk programs.
The optional file supplies debugger commands to execute non-interactively.
No space is allowed between -D and file.

option.name: --dump-variables
tip: Print a sorted list of global variables, their types and final values to file.
The default file is awkvars.out in the current directory.
No space is allowed between -d and file.

option.name: --exec
tip: Read awk program text from file, like --file.
Option processing ends here, and command-line variable assignments are disallowed.

option.name: --field-separator
tip: Set the FS variable to fs.

option.name: --file
tip: Read the awk program source from program-file instead of the first non-option argument.
May be given multiple times; the program is the concatenation of the files.

option.name: --gen-pot
tip: Analyze the source program and write a GNU gettext portable object template to standard output.
The program is not executed.

option.name: --include
tip: Read an awk source library from source-file; equivalent to the @include directive.
Files already loaded are skipped, and the source does not count as main program input.

option.name: --lint-old
tip: Warn about constructs that are not available in the original version of awk from Version 7 Unix.

option.name: --lint=
tip: Warn about constructs that are dubious or non-portable to other awk implementations.
The value is attached to the option, e.g. --lint=fatal or -Lfatal.
Possible values: fatal, invalid, no-ext

next.name: fatal
tip: Make lint warnings fatal errors.

next.name: invalid
tip: Only issue warnings about things that are actually invalid.

next.name: no-ext
tip: Disable warnings about gawk extensions.

option.name: --load
tip: Load the dynamic extension ext, searched with the AWKLIBPATH environment variable.
The platform's shared library suffix is supplied by default, so it need not be given.

option.name: --no-optimize
tip: Disable gawk's default optimizations on the internal representation of the program.

option.name: --non-decimal-data
tip: Enable automatic interpretation of octal and hexadecimal values in input data.
Can severely break old programs; use with care.

option.name: --optimize
tip: Enable gawk's default optimizations on the internal representation of the program. (enabled by default)
May be used to cancel the effect of an earlier --no-optimize.

option.name: --posix
tip: Operate in strict POSIX mode, disabling all gawk extensions.
Takes precedence over --traditional.

option.name: --pretty-print
tip: Enable pretty-printing of awk programs; the result is written to file.
The default file is awkprof.out in the current directory.
Implies --no-optimize, and no space is allowed between -o and file.

option.name: --profile
tip: Enable profiling of awk programs; the profile is written to file.
The default file is awkprof.out in the current directory.
Implies --no-optimize, and no space is allowed between -p and file.

option.name: --re-interval
tip: Allow interval expressions in regexps.
This is gawk's default; the option remains for backwards compatibility.

option.name: --sandbox
tip: Disable system(), input redirection with getline, output redirection with print and printf, and dynamic extensions.
File names may not be added to ARGV either.

option.name: --source
tip: Provide program source code in program-text, so code in files and on the command line can be mixed.
Each string is treated as if it ended with a newline and began with @namespace "awk".

option.name: --trace
tip: Print the internal byte code names as they are executed, to standard error.

option.name: --traditional
tip: Run in compatibility mode, where the GNU extensions to the awk language are disabled and gawk behaves like BWK awk.

option.name: --use-lc-numeric
tip: Force the use of the locale's decimal point character when parsing numeric input data.

option.name: -W
tip: Provide an implementation-specific option, the POSIX convention for an option that also has a GNU-style long form.
The keyword is the long option's name, so -W version is --version and -W csv is --csv.

global_option.name: --help
tip: Print a usage message summarizing the short- and long-style options gawk accepts and exit.

global_option.name: --version
tip: Print version information for this particular copy of gawk.
